title: casp schedule --json report
description: The stable machine-readable output of `casp schedule`. Reporting, never gating: this verb exits 0 on any readable cockpit, drift included. Documented in docs/schedule-json.md. `pace` is MEASURED from the git history of casp/state.json every run and is recorded nowhere — a stored pace drifts from the real one by construction. `derived` is arithmetic over that pace, never a forecast. The timeline drawing the human rendering prints is deliberately absent: a picture is not a machine contract.

schema_version.description: Bumps only on a breaking shape change; additive fields do not bump it.

today.description: The day every `state` and `days` field below was computed against.

adopted.description: false when there is no casp/schedule.json. The verb still reports pace and derived length.

malformed_detail.description: Every structural problem found, joined — one sentence per problem, never a stack.

pace.description: Measured from `git log -- casp/state.json`, reading phases_shipped.length out of each commit's blob. `measurable: false` with a `reason` whenever fewer than two usable data points exist, the window has no span, or nothing shipped in it — casp never invents a rate.

window_weeks.description: The window, anchored on `today`, not on the newest commit: a cockpit whose last state commit is six months old is not still shipping at its old pace.

walk_cap.description: Hard cap on the history walk.

derived.description: null whenever the pace is not measurable or the queue is empty. A consumer that treats this as a commitment is misreading a quotient.

claims.description: Every anchor and due recorded in the file, marked against `today`. Empty when the layer is not adopted or the file is malformed.

id.description: The anchor id, or the phase name for a due.

days.description: Signed days from today to the claim; negative once passed.

findings.description: Exactly the CASP-SCHEDULE-* findings `casp check` would emit for this cockpit. `fail` here blocks a push there; `warn` never does, and a warn caused by the clock never becomes a fail.
